title: Verify empty debug views and older runtime refusal
changes: Record candidate empty content and cheat views and unsupported-capability behavior against a real older frontend.
validation: The remapped candidate opened an empty content selector and cheat catalog on a public synthetic seed; reviewed screenshots show the refresh/add and import instructions. Frame, clock, full-state hash, registers, CPSR and keys stayed unchanged, the window closed normally and protected inputs were unchanged (dbg28-empty-compat-l50bh__p). A synthetic old-capability metadata check returned incompatible and not-sent via both clients.

A separate copied older Linux executable advertised cheat-catalog-v1 but not cheat-capabilities-v1. Both the new candidate debug-control and debug-command clients returned a clear incompatible/not-sent error without changing either mailbox or guest frame, clock, full-state hash, registers or keys. The older window closed normally and all protected originals stayed unchanged (dbg28-real-old-runtime-fixed-1rsjato1). The first driver timed out finding the old window under its newer title (nhi89gqx); the corrected title passed.
limitations: These are selected Linux/Xvfb cases with synthetic input, not all empty states or old protocol combinations. Physical controller, native Windows, the rest of DBG2-27 and release remain open. The older executable was copied read-only; its original session was not resumed.
